definition: to assess the value, quality, or worth of something
memoryTip: APPRAise the price—assess value (not the same as praise).
correctPassage: A jeweler came to appraise the necklace before the insurance renewal.
wrongPassages: Fans rose to appraise the singer with a standing ovation.
The lab will appraise contamination by leaving samples unlabeled.
She hoped the coach would appraise her effort with a public speech.

definition: to perceive, detect, or recognize with care
memoryTip: DIS-cern: sift carefully until you can tell things apart.
correctPassage: Only a trained ear can discern the slight change in pitch.
wrongPassages: The firm tried to discern open tickets by auto-closing anything over thirty days old.
They billed discern time by rounding every six-minute block upward.
The tide gauge's discern needle had been frozen mid-scale for months.

memoryTip: Con-SPIC-uous: easy to SEE (Latin spicere) because it stands out.
correctPassage: His bright red jacket made him conspicuous in the gray crowd.
wrongPassages: She kept the papers conspicuous in a locked drawer no one ever opened.
The motif sounded conspicuous after brass buried it completely.
His quiet, camouflaged outfit was designed to be as conspicuous as possible.

definition: to formally declare that one is giving something up
memoryTip: Re-NOUNCE: publicly announce you are giving it up.
correctPassage: She chose to renounce the inheritance and donate it instead.
wrongPassages: Reviewers called the stats renounce after the reanalysis matched the paper.
The empty dock looked renounce with loaders parked for a decade.
He hoped to renounce the award by accepting it on live television.

definition: a minor weakness or harmless eccentricity
memoryTip: A little FOIBLE is a foil-able flaw—minor, not fatal.
correctPassage: His only foible was humming while he graded late at night.
wrongPassages: The structural foible cracked the foundation from corner to corner.
Critics praised her foible leadership for saving the company in a crisis.
The only foible in the bridge design was a missing support beam.

definition: to express disapproval or disappointment; blame
memoryTip: Re-PROACH: approach someone again—with blame, not praise.
correctPassage: There was quiet reproach in the way she asked why he was late.
wrongPassages: Fans offered loud reproach that sounded exactly like a standing ovation.
The empty dock looked reproach with ramps chained up for years.
Her letter of reproach thanked him warmly for every favor he had done.

memoryTip: Full of CONTEMPT—scornful, looking down on someone.
correctPassage: His contemptuous shrug made it clear he thought the plan was foolish.
wrongPassages: The orchard looked contemptuous after hail stripped every tree.
She gave a contemptuous smile that radiated pure admiration.
He called the puzzle contemptuous after solving it in under a minute.

memoryTip: Makes you START (jump)—so surprising you flinch.
correctPassage: The most startling finding was that sleep alone cut errors in half.
wrongPassages: Nothing about the predictable ending felt startling to anyone in the room.
The empty stand looked startling after packing, with only chalk marks left.
Voters tabled the startling tax that every rider had already calmly expected.

definition: to fail to give a true impression of; to contradict
memoryTip: Be-LIE: the surface lies about what is really underneath.
correctPassage: His calm tone belied how nervous he felt before the exam.
wrongPassages: I fully belie the witness after checking every date in her story.
She closed the ticket as belie while action items still had no owners.
Fans found the remaster belie for files identical to the old CD.

definition: peculiar to an individual; highly distinctive
memoryTip: IDIO + quirks: your personal odd habits and style.
correctPassage: Her idiosyncratic color code made the spreadsheet unreadable to others.
wrongPassages: Everyone followed the same idiosyncratic checklist issued by headquarters.
The salt flat stayed idiosyncratic under a model with permanent drought.
The tripwire was idiosyncratic: set past any value the logs could store.
